summary: The authoritative milestone-scoped timing detector attributed 0 experiment commits, 0 wall-minutes, and 0 compute-bound tasks to 2026.06.415, so gpu_idle_on_compute_bound_tasks is null (there was no compute-bound task to assess). On-disk ground truth read this turn (ops/changelog + results/experiment_4490..4499_*.json mtimes, a ~2h23m window 04:37-07:00Z) shows the milestone actually ran exp4490-exp4499 -- all synthesis/aggregation tasks with no GGUF/CUDA markers -- so the zero is the recurring false-zero detector gap (documented across .363-.412, now extending to .415), not idle execution.
bottlenecks_identified: Observability, not speed, is the only real bottleneck: the milestone-scoped timing detector reported 0 experiment commits since activation, yet on-disk artifacts (exp4490-exp4499) and the ops/changelog window show 10 tasks executed over a ~2h23m span. This recurring false-zero gap (.363-.412, now .415) is what blocks per-experiment efficiency analysis -- there is no slow-experiment signal to flag because the timing rows never reached the retro.

GPU idle is NOT a bottleneck this milestone: a grep of the .415 window (results/experiment_449[0-9]_*.json) found no GGUF / CUDA / requires_gpu markers, so every task was synthesis/aggregation with no GPU code path. Both RTX 3090s reading 0% is correct behaviour; gpu_idle_on_compute_bound_tasks is null because compute_bound_experiments_count is 0.
improvements_suggested: Repair the milestone-scoped timing detector with a fallback: when the git-commit-attribution path returns 0 commits since activation, scan results/experiment_*.json mtimes within the activation->HEAD window and parse the ops/changelog window, so retros stop false-zeroing real work.

Emit a detector_gap_suspected=true flag whenever the commit detector reports 0 but on-disk artifacts exist in the milestone window -- convert the silent false-zero into an explicit signal the retro can branch on instead of reporting an empty milestone.

Stamp duration_s and compute_bound at artifact write-time inside the experiment template, so per-experiment timing is artifact-intrinsic and survives even when the commit-window detector misses -- removing the retro's dependence on brittle git-commit attribution.
No GPU or DualGPURunner change is warranted: 0 compute-bound and 0 multi-model-parallel tasks ran this milestone, so single-GPU and idle-GPU states are both correct.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Fix the milestone-scoped timing detector (mtime + ops/changelog-window fallback) -- it is the recurring single point of failure across .363-.415 and is what prevents any per-experiment efficiency analysis from reaching the retro.

Add write-time duration_s / compute_bound stamping in the experiment template so timing is intrinsic to each artifact rather than derived from git commits, making future retros robust to the detector gap.

Emit detector_gap_suspected=true when the detector reports 0 while on-disk artifacts exist in the window, so future retros honestly diagnose an observability gap instead of silently reporting a zero-experiment milestone.
meta_reflection: The HOW-was-it-executed question is answerable from on-disk evidence and the answer is healthy: 10 tasks (exp4490-exp4499) ran over ~2h23m, all synthesis/aggregation, with the GPUs correctly idle. The single operational defect is observability -- the timing detector false-zeroed again, the recurring failure across .363-.415 -- so the loop's weak point is measuring its own work, not doing it; making timing artifact-intrinsic is the durable fix.
